title: AW source pack
description: Schema for a sources/<region>/<name>.yaml declarative source pack (task 311, architecture.md §4.1). Schemas what M2 actually needed to codify the existing CH recipe honestly — not a speculative superset. A pack describes ONE source or one tight family of same-shape hosts (e.g. the 26 cantonal law platforms); admission is logged per POLICY.md@v1 §3 / index-governance.md §3.

id.description: Stable pack id, e.g. 'ch-fedlex'. Used as the point-id/provenance namespace anchor; never renamed once admitted (I1).

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 jurisdiction this pack primarily serves (e.g. 'CH'), or 'multi' for a cross-jurisdiction pack (e.g. an INTL broadcaster stamped CH by policy override).

layer.description: POLICY.md@v1 §4.x layer this pack is admitted under (§4.1..§4.9, in that enum order).

policy_section.description: Optional explicit POLICY.md@v1 section cite for the layer (e.g. '§4.1'), when the layer alone is ambiguous (e.g. a registry pack under §4.9 commercial vs a law pack under §4.1).

adapter.description: Adapter family per architecture.md §4.1 — the closed set of six engine concepts. A pack MAY layer a bespoke extractor (see 'extractor') on top of one family; it never invents a new family.

acquisition_policy.description: Acquisition route and vantage policy pinned by data/acquisition-policy.v1.json.

outlink_policy.description: Every source document emits resolved external links with source/context, or a receipted empty outlink stage.

preservation_profiles.description: Allowed source-preservation profiles for this pack, defined in data/source-preservation-profiles.v1.json. A mixed-route pack declares every profile it uses; each sealed release source entry selects exactly one and carries its own L0->L1->L2 receipts.

extractor.description: Optional repo-relative path to a source-specific extractor plugging into the adapter family's interface (e.g. 'cytir/sources/families/fedlex.py').

provenance.description: architecture.md §4.4 provenance class. CH packs are 'authored' (jurisdictional, hand-curated) unless explicitly noted otherwise.

tier.description: Legacy payload content-tier letter (tier=A/B/C, as stamped on records by the existing ingesters). Optional — carried for continuity with in-index payloads; not a governance instrument.

trust_tier.description: Numeric trust_tier stamped on records from this pack (0-1).

density_tier.description: POLICY.md@v1 §5 density tier this pack currently holds (T0 pointer .. T3 exhaustive). Optional: only meaningful once a pack has been through a §5/§6 assessment; a grandfathered pack may leave this unset and say so in notes.

repo_list.description: Optional repo-relative path of a JSONL file with one repository per row (owner_repo, branch, sha, license, mode, source, in_index); the github_repo_docs refresh adapter appends the rows to the routes (task 996).

theme.description: PORTFOLIO.md §3b cross-cutting theme tags (e.g. 'zero-employee-company-ops'). Optional; most CH jurisdictional packs carry none.

default.description: SPDX-style id or a short descriptive license string per ADR-039 (e.g. 'public-domain', 'CC0-1.0', 'Swiss public commercial register (Zefix/LINDAS, OGD)', 'permissive-or-fairuse-snippet').

basis.description: Consent posture per ADR-009/POLICY §2 U1. 'official-no-copyright' = amtliche Werke / no robots signal needed (URG Art.5-class). Actual search_ok/train_ok are NEVER hardcoded here — they are re-resolved live at every build (architecture §5 step 2); this field documents the pack's expected/observed posture only.

train_ok_override.description: If non-null, a build-time override forced on top of the live resolve (e.g. train_ok forced false for copyrighted broadcaster content per task 292/293 even though search_ok=true).

dense.description: What the dense channel text is built from.

sparse.description: What the sparse/BM25 channel text is built from.

card_recipe.description: Only present for adapter: cards packs (or dump/registry packs whose deliverable is entity cards).

routes.description: Sub-host/sub-jurisdiction entries for a pack that fans out over many same-shape hosts (e.g. 26 cantons). Optional — a single-host pack omits this.

route.description: DEPRECATED free prose (task 434). Human note on how the host is reached. Real config moved to `acquire`; this field is retained for continuity and must not be parsed by code.

recheck_after.description: For status deferred/declined: the date after which this route's blocker must be RE-VERIFIED rather than inherited. Adopted 2026-08-07 (task 399). A reason without a date is how a temporary block silently becomes a permanent absence: sources/igo/igo-core.yaml recorded www.iea.org as 'fully bot-blocked' on 2026-07-28, and re-verification ten days later enumerated 27,692 URLs and extracted cleanly — the largest energy-authority source in that wave had been sitting behind a stale verdict. Cadence: consent DECLINES get a long horizon (the publisher stated a preference; we re-ask rarely and respect it meanwhile), technical blocks (WAF, missing route, JS-shell) a short one.

evidence.description: Task doc / artifact this route's claim traces to, e.g. 'task 117'.

license.description: Per-route SPDX-style licence id, overriding license.default. Required when license.default is a placeholder such as 'per-route' — several packs declare that placeholder and carry the real per-host mapping only in prose `notes:`, which cannot be stamped on a record. ADR-039 requires a real per-record licence in the compact redistributable dump, so pack_loader REFUSES to stamp a placeholder.

trust_tier.description: Per-route trust_tier, overriding the pack-level value. LEGISLATIVE FIELD: trust_tier is a ranking input, so this is proposed by PR and ratified by the board, not landed direct-to-main. Rationale (task 434): several packs are a family of hosts at DIFFERENT authority levels but can only declare one number. energy-climate-intl declares trust_tier 0.95 while its ingester assigns 0.95 to IPCC (the assessment body itself) and 0.90 to IEA/EIA/UBA/EC-energy (official agencies). Without this field, migrating those packs would silently promote four official-agency hosts to treaty-body trust.

status.description: Pack-level status. For a multi-route pack this is the aggregate/headline status; per-route status lives in 'routes'.

channel.description: Discovery channel that surfaced this source, per index-governance.md §5 channel census (e.g. 'official-dump', 'aggregator-force-multiplier', 'registry-resolve', 'endorsement-frontier').

evidence.description: Pointers to the evidence this decision rests on — task docs, ADRs, measured counts. E.g. 'task 223: CC-join+slug-live recall 18.3%'.

decision.description: 'grandfathered-at-M2' = ingested before POLICY.md@v1 existed (2026-07-22); logged honestly rather than back-dated as auto-admit. See 'would_pass_today' for the retroactive check.

policy.description: Policy version [+ section] this decision is logged against, e.g. 'POLICY.md@v1 §4.1'. For grandfathered packs this cites the section they WOULD be assessed under today, per governance §3's admission-block shape.

date.description: Decision date (ingest date for grandfathered packs, ratification-adjacent date for anything assessed post-POLICY).

would_pass_today.description: For decision: grandfathered-at-M2 only — an honest self-check: does this source clear POLICY.md@v1 §2/§4/§6 as written today? false must be explained in 'notes'.

notes.description: Freeform honesty flags: gaps, ambiguities, anything that would NOT pass cleanly today, follow-ups.

acquire.description: HOW this pack (or this route) is acquired — task 434. Replaces the free-prose `routes[].route` string, which trapped real config in a sentence (ch-media.yaml: 'CC-S3 columnar, path-scoped (/news /sport /kultur)'). NOTE the level: acquisition shape belongs to a ROUTE, not a pack. ch-media reaches srf.ch/rsi.ch by common_crawl and rts.ch by sitemap — one pack, two shapes. A pack-level `acquire` is only a DEFAULT that routes may override. Vocabulary is NOT new: `route` is the ratified route_precedence enum from data/acquisition-policy.v1.json, and is orthogonal to `adapter` (which engine parses the bytes). Both are kept; neither is replaced.

route.description: Acquisition route. MUST be one of data/acquisition-policy.v1.json route_precedence[].route — validate.py cross-checks this against that file so the enum has one home, not two.

rank.description: Optional, redundant-by-design: the policy rank of `route`. If present it MUST equal the rank in acquisition-policy.v1.json. Declaring it makes a silent policy re-ranking fail loudly in pack validation.

params.description: Route-specific parameters. Allowed/required keys per route are defined once in sources/_schema/validate.py (ROUTE_PARAMS) and imported by cytir/sources/pack_loader.py — one home for the contract.

select.description: Closed predicate vocabulary replacing the Python lambdas in the HOSTS dicts. Measured over 97 predicates in the five run_pack packs: 43 were a constant lang, and the remainder reduce to exactly these four forms.

min_path_segments.description: Minimum path segments for a URL to count as an ITEM rather than a section landing page. Default in data/url-select-presets.v1.json (2). Set 0 to disable.

deny_preset.description: Named preset from data/url-select-presets.v1.json (e.g. 'generic-apparatus'). Generic site-furniture filtering is apparatus, not source config — it is declared by name so it has one home rather than being restated per pack.

lang.description: Language rule. `const` covers 43 of the 97 measured predicates; `by_path_segment` covers the multilingual CH hosts (/de/ -> de).

delay_s.description: Politeness floor. Effective delay is max(this, robots crawl-delay).

vantage.description: acquisition-policy.v1 vantage_order. The orchestration host does orchestration only (policy supersedes 2026-08-14): all source retrieval runs on the build host.

reason_receipt.description: Required by acquisition-policy.v1 direct_fetch.required_reason_fields when route=direct_origin_crawl (rank 6). Enforced WARN-ONLY at first (orchestrator ruling 2026-08-20): 16 existing scripts owe one, and a validator that fails everything on day one gets disabled by the next person in a hurry.

extractor.description: Route-level override of the pack-level `extractor` — the escape hatch for genuinely bespoke dialects (DE Genesis, FR DILA, StatCan WDS), per architecture.md §4.1 'adapter honesty' (F5).

engine.description: Dispatch engine for this route. `default` selects the shared engine implied by `route`; `extractor` deliberately delegates even sitemap/direct-crawl enumeration to the declared extractor when that extractor implements a richer, already-proven family contract. This is explicit because the presence of a pack-level extractor alone is not enough: authority packs still use pack_fetch for their sitemap routes.

config_ref.description: Exact extractor-owned configuration entry backing this route. The source runner passes it through the aw.source-extractor-env.v1 contract; it is data provenance, not a second copy of the extractor config.

no_fallback.description: A binding commitment that this source is acquired ONLY by its declared route and is never crawled. Requested as a hard requirement by the company-register lane: the Canadian pack commits to never crawling the HTML detail pages. Enforced in TWO places, because a promise a tool cannot check is just a comment: sources/_schema/validate.py rejects a pack that sets no_fallback while declaring a crawl route, and cytir/sources/runner.py refuses at run time to dispatch such a pack to a crawl engine.
